work_completed: AGENT-LOOP-002 T3 (engine-owned scene transition), asked for by Joshua 2026-10-18.

WorldView.ShowScene returns bool: false and nothing changed when a --scene pin holds the view, the id names no interior level, or the level fails to load. The level is loaded before the open world is switched off. Read-only accessors added: WorldPortals, PinnedSceneId, InteriorLevelExists.

AgentBrain: one placement path, PlaceAt (position, zero velocity, LocomotionController.Teleport, held decision cleared). TransitionTo(position, sceneId, facing) and the kill plane both use it; HoldForTransition/ReleaseHold freeze the body while scenes swap. The kill plane recovers indoors to InteriorRecoveryPoint (the room's arrival point). The comment records the approval (Joshua 2026-10-17) and the AGENTS.md rule it is the exception to.
AvatarCharacter.ApplyIntent takes an onArrival callback, run on arrival or at once when already at the target; OnPlaced turns the visual to the given facing and returns to the wander fallback.

SceneTransitRules (new, SceneTransit.cs): the ingress check for a doorway (busy, capture pin, unknown scene, unknown building, missing interior level) and the arrival points (inside: the room's exit anchor facing in; outside: the building's Portal.EntryPoint facing out). SceneAnchorSets uses the same indoor point, so an avatar that has just entered stands on the exit.

IntentIngress: `use` on a doorway asks IPortalTransit.CanTransit before the avatar walks (refusal = rejection with reason, avatar not moved; no transit available = rejected, fail closed), passes Transit as the arrival callback, and logs each accepted transition as a new class of physical effect. Any intent arriving mid-transition is rejected.

Main implements IPortalTransit: deferred RunTransit holds the avatar, makes physics follow the destination (OpenWorldBodiesLive follows the loop avatar's scene or its destination), shows it, waits two physics frames, ray-casts the floor (AvatarGround y = 0 backstop indoors, terrain outside), places the avatar, swaps its wander anchors (none indoors), and warns about any other physical avatar left in the switched-off scene. On failure the avatar is released where it stood and the previous scene is shown again.
work_in_progress: AGENT-LOOP-002 T4-T6 next, in this session.
decisions_made: The transition is checked at ingress, before the avatar walks, so a doorway that cannot be used is a rejected intent with a reason rather than a walk that ends in nothing. A level that fails to load after acceptance is handled by ShowScene's safe failure: the avatar is released where it stood.
Inside a room the wander fallback gets no anchors, so it roams the room instead of heading for the exit (the only room anchor today).

Out-of-reach rejection for a door cannot arise on this path: perception range (25 m) is below the reach check (30 m), so a door the model can name is always within reach; a door it cannot see is rejected by protocol validation ('target not in perception').
